entries.prompt:
Use case: style-transfer. Asset type: original monster RPG pixel-art sprite sheet with TWO authored views of the SAME reference creature, used in a released browser game. Input image is the precise character-design reference; preserve its identity, silhouette, anatomy, colors and distinctive markings.
Primary request: convert this reference monster into exceptionally clean crisp 16-bit pixel art, and author its genuine back view. SMALL BASE FORM: chubby adorable turquoise/teal seal-walrus cub, big round head, two large amber eyes, tiny translucent cyan icy tusks, white sweeping little hair tuft marked with a turquoise V, tiny foreflippers with white tips, pale mint belly, small split tail. Preserve the cute compact anatomy of input 4.png.
Composition: wide 2:1 transparent canvas divided conceptually into two equal square cells, with no drawn dividing line. In LEFT HALF show ONE full-body FRONT three-quarter view, facing SCREEN LEFT so eyes/nose aim left. In RIGHT HALF show ONE full-body REAR three-quarter view, facing SCREEN RIGHT, looking away from viewer; show the actual back of head, back, limbs and tail, not the front mirrored and not a second front face. Match body scale and baseline between views. Center each figure in its own half, entire silhouette visible, about 76% of cell height, at least 8% completely clear padding on every cell edge. Ensure a wide completely transparent central gutter, no limbs crossing halves.
Style: meticulously clustered pixel art intended to read cleanly at 160x160 game pixels per creature, obvious square pixel steps, limited cohesive palette, dark 1-pixel silhouette outline, controlled 3-to-5 shade ramps, no smooth photographic textures, no blur or antialiasing. Maintain the reference's exact creature features; do not invent armor accessories, horns or extra limbs.
Background: actual transparent alpha across all empty pixels. No ground, cast shadow, scenery, checkerboard texture, text, labels, watermark, border or UI. Only TWO complete creature sprites.
